questions.key_step: Parabola-line intersections, integrate difference.
questions.justification: Single standard move (area between a parabola and a line); nothing to decide. Easier than 2021-P1-Q2 (L2) which had four bounding curves.

questions.key_step: Normal of slope -1 means tangent slope 1, then parabola-chord area.
questions.justification: Three routine stages (point, normal, area) with no insight; same demand as 2024-P2-Q2 (L2).

questions.key_step: y dy = dx gives y^2=2x, then area with x=2.
questions.justification: Separable DE then a standard parabola segment; routine chain, numerical answer p+q.

questions.key_step: Rotate tangent by -pi/4 via tan(theta-pi/4), then chord area.
questions.justification: Angle subtraction, Vieta for the second root, exact fraction in a numerical answer (precision risk F2); a step longer than Q2-Q3.

questions.key_step: Equal-area condition gives (1-a)^3=8; area of second region in y.
questions.justification: Two areas, one integrating in y, plus greatest-integer cosmetic; two linked ideas but each standard.

questions.key_step: cos^-1|cos x| = x on [0,pi/2]; crossing at x=1 splits the integral.
questions.justification: Reading the inverse-trig graph and noticing the crossing inside the interval; ill-posed 'minimum' wording adds ambiguity.

questions.key_step: Polynomial difference equation gives x^2+1; tangents y=+-2x.
questions.justification: Several routine parts (find f, tangents, area) with no real insight; multi-part subjective.

questions.key_step: Leibniz/L'Hopital on integral over t^3.
questions.justification: One familiar move after writing the two areas.

questions.key_step: A(n)=(n-1)/(2n(n+1)), maximise in n.
questions.justification: Tangent, intercept, area and a derivative test; chain of routine steps, answer n=1+sqrt2.

questions.key_step: Differentiate A1(a) to get f(a)=a sin a; then three by-parts areas.
questions.justification: Needs the idea of treating A1 as a function of a and differentiating; then precision in A2, A3 with signs.

questions.key_step: Touching curves, ln-integrals, solve ln(a-1)=2 and ln(b-1)=-2.
questions.justification: Two parts with logarithmic antiderivatives and sign checks; precision rather than insight.

questions.key_step: Maximum at x=e^{1+c}, area (ln x - c)^2/2.
questions.justification: Short chain with the substitution ln x - c; 'show independent of c' form.

questions.key_step: Case analysis on a with the asymptote x=1/2 and crossing at x=1.
questions.justification: Four cases (a>2, 1<a<2, 1/2<a<1, a<1/2) each with its own quadratic, and an infinite-area case that is easy to miss; no options to check against (F2).

questions.key_step: Area = pi/2 - alpha/(1+alpha^2), minimise.
questions.justification: Area minus two triangles, arctan identity, derivative; three linked steps.

questions.key_step: A = D^{3/2}/6 with D=m^2-4m+4c; minimise over m.
questions.justification: Long algebra for the area as a function of m and then a minimisation, answer built from c and m.

questions.key_step: tan^n+tan^{n-2}=tan^{n-2}sec^2; monotonic bounds.
questions.justification: Prove-type with a reduction identity and a two-sided monotonic bound; two linked ideas.

questions.key_step: Equal-area condition gives sin(alpha/2)=1/2; ratio of areas above and below y=1.
questions.justification: Two parts; the second needs the intersections of both cosines with y=1 and four sub-integrals with exact surds (F2).

questions.key_step: Split at x=a as f is decreasing; A'(a)=a(2a-1)/sqrt(1-a^2).
questions.justification: Three outputs (min, local max, absolute max) with end-point comparison; a slip in the area function wrecks everything, as the printed solution shows.

questions.key_step: Equal areas for every P: differentiate in alpha and invert f.
questions.justification: Unfamiliar functional-integral idea (differentiate the area identity, use the inverse function); the algebra is short once seen.

questions.key_step: Spot e^x(h+h') pattern twice.
questions.justification: Recognising the pattern twice (for f and for f-g); then a one-line evaluation.

questions.key_step: Differentiate the integral equation: f'=x/3.
questions.justification: Leibniz differentiation, cancel f^2, integrate; routine.
One standard formula and a direct integral.

questions.key_step: dy/dx infinite at 0: use x as a function of y.
questions.justification: The twist of using formula (ii) is the only decision; arithmetic is routine.

questions.key_step: 1+y'^2 is the perfect square (x^2+1)^2.
questions.justification: Compute y', spot the perfect square, integrate; mildly routine.

questions.key_step: f'(x)=e^x+f(x) from the definition; solve to xe^x; sign of f'.
questions.justification: Functional equation to ODE to extrema; three linked stages and a differentiability subtlety.

questions.key_step: Global minimum -1/e and f->inf.
questions.justification: Follows from the previous part; one standard range argument.

questions.key_step: x e^x -> 0 as x -> -inf.
questions.justification: One familiar limit.

questions.key_step: Bounded region only for x<=0; improper integral of -x e^x.
questions.justification: Improper integral and a decision about which region is bounded; routine antiderivative.

questions.key_step: Four standard areas; cubic with sign changes.
questions.justification: Four short routine items with elimination possible (MTC average 2.1).

questions.key_step: (C) exact derivative of (sin x)^{cos x}; (D) bound f'<=2/x.
questions.justification: Four items from four chapters; (C) and (D) need non-routine ideas (an exact derivative of u^v, a differential inequality), as in 2026-P1-Q15 (matching with an idea) rated 4.

questions.key_step: Regions with [x]=[y], modulus and circle; (D) lobes minus segments.
questions.justification: Four sketch-based items; (D) needs the lobes-minus-circle-segments picture and exact area bookkeeping.
